sections.html:
Cottonwood Heights is a city on the east bench of the Salt Lake Valley in Salt Lake County, south of Holladay and Murray, east of Midvale and north of Sandy. Its official nickname is the City between the canyons.

A high ridge separates the Big Cottonwood and Little Cottonwood creek valleys, and at the eastern edge both valleys narrow into canyons in the Wasatch Mountains. The elevation is about 4,820 feet, and the city covers 9.23 square miles. Interstate 215 runs along the northern border, and State Routes 190 and 210 reach the canyon mouths near the eastern edge.

Salt Lake County itself held 1,185,238 people in 2020. Big Cottonwood Canyon leads to the Solitude and Brighton ski resorts, and Little Cottonwood Canyon leads to Snowbird and Alta, so the city sits at the doorway to winter recreation.

sections.h2: When did Cottonwood Heights become a city?
sections.html:
Cottonwood Heights was an unincorporated area until voters approved a referendum in May 2004, and the city incorporated on January 14, 2005. On January 8, 2008, the city council voted to start its own police department and leave the Salt Lake County Sheriff's contract.

The area's roots go back further. An old paper mill, the Cottonwood Paper Mill, was built in 1883 by the Deseret News. The city is also building a multi-use trail along Big Cottonwood Creek within its borders.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 32,265. The city has 12,762 households and 13,536 housing units, with 5.7 percent vacant, and a median age of 39.1. About 18.4 percent of residents are 65 or older, which fits a city where many owners have lived in the same house for a long time.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Cottonwood Heights gets about 25.9 inches of precipitation a year. April is the wettest month at 3.49 inches and July the driest at 0.92 inches, based on the 1991 to 2020 normals.

Lots near the canyon mouths can see snowmelt run toward foundations in spring. Houses near the creeks should be checked for grading, window wells and sump pumps. Steeper streets can also mean retaining walls that age and lean.

  • Spring runoff near Big and Little Cottonwood creeks
  • Window wells and basement drainage
  • Retaining walls and sloped driveways
  • Roof and gutter wear after heavy snow

The Wasatch Fault runs along the mountain front. The Utah Division of Emergency Management says more than 85 percent of Utahns live in the earthquake zone, and it highlights older unreinforced masonry buildings as the greatest concern. Strapping water heaters and checking chimneys are simple steps to take before a sale.

Cottonwood Heights has a business base unusual for a suburb, with several corporate offices inside city limits. Instructure, Dyno Nobel, Extra Space Storage, Breeze Airways and JetBlue all have offices in the city.

Salt Lake County has long relied on church-related services and mining, and now depends on defense industries, tourism and winter sports, and service and technology firms. Many residents commute across the valley. Salt Lake City International Airport is the county's only airport with scheduled passenger service, and TRAX light rail and FrontRunner serve other parts of the county.

City Hall has a Community and Economic Development department with a business development specialist on staff, so a company with questions about a property used for work can start there.

sections.h2: Which public schools serve Cottonwood Heights?
sections.html:
Cottonwood Heights belongs to the Canyons School District. The district lists five schools in the city, and the district office is at 9361 South 300 East in Sandy.

SchoolLevel
Butler Elementary (dual immersion)Elementary
Canyon View ElementaryElementary
Ridgecrest Elementary (dual immersion)Elementary
Butler MiddleMiddle
Brighton HighHigh

Brighton High is the city's only public high school, and Butler Middle is its only public middle school. The district runs a School Finder tool for checking boundaries by address, which buyers often use before they make an offer.

sections.h2: What local rules affect a seller in Cottonwood Heights?
sections.html:
The city office at 2277 Bengal Boulevard handles planning, zoning, building permits and inspections, and the main number is 801-944-7000. Code enforcement is listed under the police department.

The city has its own short-term rental ordinance, and a license is required. The city allows them mainly in multi-family residential areas, within condominium or homeowners association communities. If you own a unit that has been used as a short-term rental, confirm the license status before you sell.

  • Building permits: check that finished basements, decks and additions were permitted
  • Accessory dwelling units: the city has its own ADU rules
  • Short-term rentals: licensed only in approved areas
  • Landscaping: the city has ordinances for outdoor lighting, trees and park strips

Unpermitted work does not stop a cash sale, but it can stop a financed one. Sorting out what has permits can save time if you plan to list with an agent.

sections.h2: How does Salt Lake County bill property tax in Cottonwood Heights?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County bills Cottonwood Heights property tax, and the last day to pay without a penalty is November 30. The county mails valuation notices around July 22 and official tax notices by November 1.

Salt Lake County dateEvent
July 22Notices of Valuation mailed
November 1Tax notices mailed
November 30Last day to pay without penalty
December 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
January 31Penalty rises from 1 percent to 2.5 percent
Fourth Thursday of MayFinal tax sale

The county gives a primary residence a 45 percent reduction, and a dwelling must be a primary home occupied at least 183 consecutive days in a year. Vacation rentals, second homes and cabins do not qualify. Owners whose mailing address differs from the property address get a letter and have 30 days to file the declaration, or the exemption is removed. The declaration also creates a presumption of Utah residency for income tax purposes, so speak with a tax professional if that matters.

sections.h2: What do Cottonwood Heights sellers typically face?
sections.html:
Sellers in Cottonwood Heights are often long-time owners, heirs or landlords with a house that needs updating. A cash sale lets them close on their own schedule, without staging, showings or repair negotiations.

  • Long-held homes with original systems that buyers want updated
  • Hillside or canyon-side lots with drainage questions
  • Estates where heirs live out of state
  • Rental or former short-term rental units with permit or license questions

With nearly one in five residents aged 65 or older, many sales follow a change in circumstances. That includes downsizing, a move, or the loss of a family member.

faqs.q: What county is Cottonwood Heights in?
faqs.a: Cottonwood Heights is in Salt Lake County, and the county treasurer bills the property tax. Valuation notices go out around July 22, and the payment deadline is November 30.
The Canyons School District serves Cottonwood Heights. The city has Butler Elementary, Canyon View Elementary, Ridgecrest Elementary, Butler Middle and Brighton High.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Cottonwood Heights?
faqs.a: Short-term rentals need a city license and are allowed mainly in multi-family residential areas within condominium or HOA communities. Ask city staff whether a specific property is eligible.

faqs.q: How does the primary residence reduction work in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County gives a 45 percent reduction in taxable value to a primary residence occupied at least 183 consecutive days in a year. Vacation homes and second homes do not qualify.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cottonwood Heights house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, a house can be sold as it is, including work done without a permit. Tell the buyer what was done, since permit status can affect financing and later inspections.
